source_text: CUM moneat Dominus et dicat: Vos estis sal terrae, cumque esse nos jubeat ad innocentiam simplices, et tamen cum simplicitate prudentes, quid aliud, fratres dilectissimi, quam providere nos convenit, et sollicito corde vigilantes, subdoli hostis insidias intelligere pariter et cavere ne qui Christum sapientiam Dei Patris induimus, minus sapere in tuenda salute videamur? Neque enim persecutio sola metuenda est et ea quae subruendis ac dejiciendis Dei servis aperta impugnatione grassantur. Facilior cautio est ubi manifesta formido est, et ad certamen animus ante praestruitur quando se adversarius confitetur. Plus metuendus est et cavendus inimicus cum latenter obrepit, cum, per pacis imaginem fallens, occultis accessibus serpit; unde et nomen serpentis accepit. Ea est ejus semper astutia, ea est circumveniendi hominis caeca et latebrosa fallacia. Sic ab initio statim mundi fefellit, et, verbis mendacibus blandiens, rudes animas incauta credulitate decepit. Dominum ipsum tentare conatus, quasi obreperet rursus et falleret, latenter accessit. Intellectus tamen est et retusus; et ideo prostratus, quia agnitus atque detectus.
pass_a_gloss: When the Lord warns and says: You are the salt of the earth, and commands us to be simple in innocence, and yet prudent with simplicity, what else is fitting for us, most beloved brothers, than to be provident, and with a solicitous heart, watchful, to understand and beware of the insidious plots of the cunning enemy equally? For not only persecution is to be feared, and those things that with open attack rage against the servants of God to subvert and cast down. Easier is caution where manifest fear is, and the mind is prepared beforehand for the contest when the adversary confesses. More to be feared and avoided is the enemy when he secretly creeps, when, deceiving by the image of peace, he slips in with hidden approaches; whence also he has received the name of serpent. This is always his cunning, this is the blind and hidden deceit of circumventing man. Thus from the beginning of the world he deceived, and, flattering with lying words, deceived rude souls with unguarded credulity. He even tried to tempt the Lord himself, and, as if he would creep again and deceive, approached secretly. Nevertheless, he was understood and repelled; and therefore, he was prostrated, because he was recognized and detected.

pass_b_english: When the Lord warns us, saying, "You are the salt of the earth," and commands us to be simple in innocence and yet prudent with simplicity, what else is fitting for us, most beloved brothers, than to be provident and, with a solicitous heart, watchful, to understand and beware of the insidious plots of the cunning enemy equally? (Matthew 5:13) For not only persecution is to be feared, nor only those things that with open attack rage against the servants of God to subvert and cast them down. Caution is easier where fear is manifest, and the mind is prepared beforehand for the contest when the adversary reveals himself. The enemy is more to be feared and avoided when he secretly creeps up, when, deceiving by the image of peace, he slips in with hidden approaches; hence he has also received the name of serpent. This is always his cunning; this is the blind and hidden deceit of circumventing man. Thus from the beginning of the world he deceived, and, flattering with lying words, deceived rude souls with unguarded credulity. He even tried to tempt the Lord himself, and, as if he would creep up again and deceive, approached secretly. Nevertheless, he was understood and repelled; and therefore he was prostrated, because he was recognized and detected.
